# The Fell Brethren

*Pages PDF 76-82*

## **The Fell Brethren**
## **All Hands on Deck**
_Temple of Spite_ is an almighty fortress ship and, like any oceangoing vessel, it needs a crew to man the defences, tend to the sails and rigging, and keep the decks in order. The ark is home to over a thousand souls, and while the swashbuckling corsairs of the raiding fleet take much of the glory, it is the crew aboard _Temple of Spite_ that keep it shipshape. There are several corsair companies posted on the ark, hardened sailors and marines dedicated to their duties, and the Fell Brethren are one such company. 

Under Captain Jareth Brackblood, the Fell Brethren command a crew assigned to undertake mundane tasks disdained by corsairs, such as setting the sails, running errands, and swabbing the decks. In a boarding action, the Fell Brethren shove these underlings aside to fight, swarming onto any enemy ship foolish enough to approach the ark, or defending the battlements with their blades and reaper bolt throwers mounted along the gunwales. 

There is no love lost between the Fell Brethren and the raiding fleet’s corsairs. The latter disparage them as menials, safe behind the walls of the ark, with none of the flair or glamour of a raiders’ life. In turn, the Brethren seethe at the arrogant glory seekers who enjoy the fleetmaster’s favour and sit on the Reavers’ Council. Brackblood and his closest compatriots feel this resentment more than most. They are veteran corsairs who supported the failed mutiny against Duriath Helbane and must now keep their treachery secret, or suffer agonising execution. 

Yet they still plot to escape _Temple of Spite_ for a new command, to receive the gratitude and spoils to which they feel entitled. 

## **Goals**
The Fell Brethren have a duty to the fleetmaster and _Temple of Spite_ and, on the surface, they act accordingly. 

**Keep the ark running efficiently.** The Fell Brethren are proud of their reputation as seafarers. They strive to keep their parts of the ark in a seaworthy state, from the decks and ramparts to the reaper bolt throwers and foresail. If the fleetmaster decides to inspect the ark, the Fell Brethren want him to have no complaints about their performance. 

**Identify and repel threats.** The Fell Brethren are warriors and sailors. They scrutinise the ocean for ships, hazards, and sea monsters and send messages to the fleetmaster should they detect any threats or potential prey. If the ark is attacked, they take the first line of defence and fight with reaper bolt throwers, crossbows, and cutlasses to repel enemy vessels and boarders. 

**Improve their standing.** While corsairs have an exalted status on the black ark, the Fell Brethren do not have the prestige of the raiding crews. Captain Brackblood and his company want to prove their invaluable role to _Temple of Spite_ and its conquests through displays of competence and flair, as well as undermining the reputation of captains on the Reavers’ Council. 

**Keep their treachery secret.** Captain Brackblood and his close confidantes supported the failed mutiny and have thus far escaped detection by the fleetmaster. Most of their coconspirators were executed, and they are eager to eliminate any who might reveal their secret. 

**Become reavers.** A minority of the Fell Brethren would rather join the raiding fleet than continue serving on the black ark, though this is something they would never confess to Captain Brackblood and his entourage. Given the opportunity, they will join the crew of a ravenship in a heartbeat and hope Brackblood is powerless to retaliate. 

**Find new masters.** Dispirited by the failed mutiny, Brackblood, along with his compatriots Velkar and Morikar Duskmere, intends to swear allegiance to another fleetmaster. They will jump ship unless Helbane loses command soon. 

## **On the Black Ark**
The Fell Brethren play an important role on _Temple of Spite_ and they know it. Defending the ark involves more than repelling boarders, and Brackblood’s corsairs patrol their territory to uncover interlopers or misbehaving inhabitants, performing a similar function to a town guard or watch. They act with haughty authority, and with the exception of Druchii highborn or member of the Black Convocation, they treat anyone straying onto their decks with little respect. The corsairs like to stop just short of violence when confronted with other corsairs or the warhost’s warriors, though they make very clear that such interlopers are merely tolerated in the Fell Brethren’s territory. 

Despite Brackblood’s misgivings, the fleetmaster does value the Fell Brethren and their fellow ark crew companies. Helbane knows _Temple of Spite_ could not survive without their efforts, and they have more prestige than they recognise. For example, when fresh captives come to the ark, the highborn select their favourites, then the black ark corsair companies are permitted to demand any captives they deem useful, though they prefer to take captured seafarers. 

## **Rivals and Allies**
The Tempest Lodge houses both the Fell Brethren and the Daughters of the Abyss, a predominantly female company of corsairs with similar responsibilities on the ark. They spend little time together, though they will ally against outsiders, and Captain Velrissa Seaglaive is on good terms with Brackblood. The Brethren’s traditional rivals are an equivalent company on the starboard side called the Night’s Wrath. Swaggering Rhaedrin Irontide likes to bait the Fell Brethren by suggesting they lack finesse and seamanship. It would not take much to bring the two companies to blows. 

The Fell Brethren have an ongoing hatred for the Spears of the Drowned Moon, a regiment of dreadspears billeted in the Bladesong Hold. Relations between the warhost and corsairs are often fraught but, in this case, the Brethren’s loathing originates from the dreadspears’ delight in killing mutineers, which took the lives of many of Brackblood’s fellow conspirators. The Spears remain suspicious of the Brethren and crave evidence of their former treachery. Other surviving mutineers live in constant fear, haunted by one another’s silence, and the Fell Brethren watch carefully for signs that another traitor is about to make a move and denounce them, hoping to pre-empt the accusations. 

A blackmailer somewhere on the ark sends messages to Brackblood about the mutiny, demanding favours such as eliminating a specific dark elf or allowing an indiscretion on their territory. This is Lady Karasashalla, who also blackmails Captain Filvanir of the _Nightwake_ for the same reason. Brackblood and Filvanir dislike one other, though they do not realise they face the same predicament. If they learn that they share a tormentor, they would ally against Karasashalla. 

Several darkshard regiments and the Brethren share mutual respect, recognising one another as expert marksmen. They sometimes hold friendly contests of skill, such as determining who can pincushion a fleeing captive from 50 paces. 

## **Internal Tensions**
Discontent grows amongst the Fell Brethren as Jareth Brackblood plans to desert the _Temple of Spite_ and take his crew with him. He intends to join another fleetmaster or dreadlord and has made subtle enquiries to emissaries from Fleetmaster Kaelleth Flayheart, a dynamic corsair prince and master of his own black ark, _Sorrowthorn_ . 

Not all the Brethren feel the same way, however. Corsairs Druveth Bane and Vexara Kintearer would prefer to join a raiding crew and are persuading their fellows to accompany them. They need someone to approach Captain Redthorn or Flariel on their behalf. Should any corsair leave the Fell Brethren company, they risk the other side of the split revealing their role in the failed mutiny. 

## **Meeting the Fell Brethren**
If the Characters try to board the ark on the port side, they meet the Fell Brethren head on. If they attempt to scale the walls ,the corsairs are waiting on the ramparts. If they assault _Temple of Spite_ with cannon or missile fire, the Fell Brethren return fire with reaper bolt throwers and prepare a party to board the Characters’ vessel. 

Aboard the ark, Characters could encounter the Brethren patrolling the decks and corridors close to the Fleetmaster’s Bastion. They will need swift, persuasive arguments or credible protection from a powerful patron to avoid conflict. The Brethren attack anyone suspicious, restrain them, and drag them to the captives’ cells. 

The Brethren oversee a small crew of captives, and Characters could be assigned to their command. Between backbreaking labour and humiliating cruelties, the corsairs could decide they look capable of more complex tasks, such as discrediting other reavers, carrying messages, or running errands. Brackblood, Soulbane, and the other Fell Brethren will not trust them with anything too risky, as they do not expect the Characters to succeed or care much if they fail. After all, they can always replace them. 

## **Appearance**
The Fell Brethren wear traditional corsairs’ sea dragon cloaks, with clothing and enamelled armour in a muted purple hue. They eschew shields and wear the insignia of their company, a skull-faced merwyrm, inscribed on their breastplates. 

The sailors wrap themselves in thick, practical clothes as proof against the elements. Captives wear whatever they can scavenge and are branded with the Fell Brethren’s insignia on their necks. 

## **Loose Lips Sink Ships — Easy Encounter**
The wind howls against the black ark, as waves lash the stonework, witchfire lanterns sway in the gloom, and four corsairs stand guard over a human lashed to a capstan. The captive’s face is bruised and bleeding. He is apparently a prisoner with something to hide, but is not yet broken. Velkar Duskmere calmly demands the captive reveal what he saw or heard. 

## **Disposition**
The Fell Brethren consists of 34 corsairs, overseeing 27 dark elf sailors and around 32 captives, although these numbers vary with attrition. 

- **Captain Jareth Brackblood** leads the company from his wardroom in Greymourn’s Turret, which projects from the ark’s ramparts 

The Characters arrive as the Brethren discuss what to do. The captive, Lars, was trying to avoid work when he saw a dark elf messenger affix a blackmail letter to Brackblood’s wardroom door. Now Velkar insists Lars help them discover the messenger’s identity. The other corsairs grow tired of interrogation and want to execute Lars for shirking. The captive pleads for his life, understanding just enough Druhir to grasp the situation. 

The corsairs need to make a decision quickly. The Characters could attack, hoping to free Lars or simply avoid their own capture. They might weigh in on the argument (especially if in disguise), or suggest _they_ know something of value to the Fell Brethren. If they are cunning, they might stoke the dispute and take advantage of the discord. 

- **Velkar** and **Morikar Duskmere** carry the company standard and warhorn respectively. The brothers are amongst Brackblood’s closest companions. Morikar uses the warhorn to signal the the company on foggy nights. 

- **Azaeril Blightfrost, Serika Malbeth,** and **Rhyssar the Pale** are Brackblood’s other confidantes — they trust one another as much as any dark elf can. Serika generally takes charge of the sailors, while Azaeril bullies the captives. 

If Lars survives the encounter, he reveals that the dark elf messenger had one milk-white pupil. This was Essir, Lady Karashalla’s servant. The corsairs do not realise that Lars also overheard Velkar and Brackblood discussing the letter and learned that they are both survivors of the failed mutiny. 

- 22 Corsairs form the bulk of the company. They routinely patrol the ark in gangs of three or four. 

- 6 Corsairs are assigned to three reaper bolt throwers on the ark’s battlements, directed by **Demeth Soulbane** . 

- 27 Dark Elf Sailors report to the Fell Brethren. 

- 32 captives cower under the Brethren’s dominion. 

## **Fracas on Deck — Medium Encounter**
The Characters are near the Tempest Lodge when they witness a tense confrontation between two groups of corsairs. In a narrow alley lined with coiled chains, a patrol of eight Fell Brethren have cornered five corsairs from the Night’s Wrath company. Captain Irontide’s elves were allegedly caught sabotaging one of the Fell Brethren’s reaper bolt throwers, or so the Brethren claim. 

Demeth Soulbane leads her fellow corsairs in demanding the Night’s Wrath elves submit to punishment. The accused insist they were framed, and Soulbane planted evidence to discredit her rivals. Both groups have weapons drawn but are yet to come to blows. Behind the Fell Brethren, three dark elf sailors watch nervously, ready to assist their masters if violence erupts. 

This encounter could unfold in several ways. If the Characters present an obvious threat to the ark, the corsairs band together and attack them, hoping to capture more captives that they can sell to the beastmasters. 

Otherwise, a large or powerful party could tip the balance in a fight. Demeth Soulbane may assume they are mere captives or servants of an important dark elf. Either way, she orders them to help restrain the alleged saboteurs and promises they will earn favour with Captain Brackblood. The Night’s Wrath corsairs counter by appealing to the Characters to help them escape injustice in exchange for the patronage of Captain Irontide. Of course, they do not admit that they did, in fact, sabotage the bolt thrower. 

## **Stop Right There! — Hard Encounter**
One of the Fell Brethren’s lookouts spotted the Characters and raised the alarm. Now the corsairs are in pursuit, with the party fleeing across the busy decks of the black ark at twilight. They must escape or find some way to distract or deter their pursuers. 

The corsairs know the layout of the ark intimately, though there are dark alleys and hidden doorways where concealment is still possible. Two harpies flap overhead, excited by the chase and eager to join the hunt. They signal when they spot the Characters by shrieking and diving towards their position. The Fell Brethren attempt to surround the Characters, using quiet routes to encircle their position. To do this, the corsairs split into smaller groups of three or four, with each patrol competing to apprehend the Characters. 

Escape is challenging, though not impossible. Fleeing into the Chainspire or the Depths takes the Brethren away from their home territory and may bring them into conflict with other factions on the ark. The Fell Brethren’s arrogance encourages them to attempt flashy, daring leaps and showy swordsmanship in competition with one another. There is a chance that a cocksure band of corsairs could slip up, let the Characters escape, and then avoid telling their compatriots out of shame. 

- Jareth Brackblood accompanied by Azaeril Blightfrost, Serika Malbeth, and 16 other Corsairs 

- 2 Harpies 

- **Fell Brethren:** 7 Corsairs and Demeth Soulbane, accompanied by three Dark Elf Sailors 

- **Night’s Wrath:** 5 Night’s Wrath Corsairs 

## **Mathlann, Lord of the Deeps**
Mathlann is the King of Storm and Sea, the ruler of the savage creatures of the deeps. he is an unpredictable deity, as likely to bestow curses as he is to grant favours, and seemingly makes no distinction between the various races of elves, only seeing a distinction between those who plough his beloved seas, and those who prefer to remain bound to dry land. 

Black ark corsairs revere Mathlann most highly. In part, this is simply good sense, as any elf who spends so much of his life upon the waves is well-advised to ensure he remains in good standing with the King of Storm and Sea. however, the corsairs also feel a kinship with Mathlann that transcends mere worship, for they too are a force of destruction that strikes without warning from calm seas, bringing rain to fleets, ports, and coastlines. 

## **Areth Brackblood, J Frustrated Mutineer**
Brackblood has spent hundreds of years watching less competent corsairs rise through the ranks, while he dutifully tends to the defence and smooth running of the ark. As a young corsair under Dravis Helbane, his future rise seemed inevitable: join a raiding ship, grow wealthy, become a captain and eventually a fleetmaster. Under Duriath Helbane’s yoke, he barely earned command of his crew and has seen no progress for 154 years. One failed mutiny later, and he has decided it is time for a change of allegiance.

Last time the ark was in Clar Karond, Brackblood ventured into a shadowy dockside tavern to meet with a representative of Prince Kaelleth Flayheart. Hekketh the Bleak told the corsair captain that his master is assembling a warhost aboard the _Sorrowthorn_ , hoping to raid the coast of Lustria. The Fell Brethren will have a place, and a ravenship, amongst Flayheart’s Reavers if they bring a small fortune to the fleetmaster’s mansion in Clar Karond. 

Brackblood wears a convincing mask as a loyal subject of Helbane. He can be charming and steely as required and exhibits the cruel bonhomie characteristic amongst dark elves in command. His face bears scars and weathering from many years at sea.

## **Traits and Talents**
**Hatred (High Elves):** See _Hatred_ in the **WFRP Core Rulebook** . 

**Night Vision:** See clearly for 20 yards and extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards. 

**Catfall:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Athletics Test related to falling or keeping their balance, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Combat Reflexes:** Combat Initiative counts as 80. 

**Dual Wielder:** When fighting with two weapons the character does not have to lose Advantage in order to make a free attack with their second weapon. 

**Furious Assault:** Once per Round, if the character hits an opponent in melee, they may immediately lose Advantage to make an extra attack. 

**Inspiring:** Can influence 5 times the normal number of followers with Leadership Skill during battle. 

**Menacing:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Intimidate Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Old Salt:** On successful Row or Sail Tests on the ocean, they may either use their rolled SL, or the number rolled on the units die. They count as two crew towards the minimum number needed to man an ocean-going vessel. **Pilot:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Row or Sail Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1. 

**Read/Write:** Can read and write. 

**Strong Swimmer:** May reverse the dice roll of any failed Swim Test, but if they do, the maximum SL they can achieve is 1.

## **Demeth Soulbane, Bolt Thrower Commander**
Demeth Soulbane earned her reputation through an almost preternatural marksmanship that borders on the uncanny. She treats reaper bolt throwers like surgical instruments, calculating trajectories with mathematical certainty even as the ark pitches beneath her feet. Her crew whispers that she can feel the wind’s intention and read the ocean’s rhythm, and they speak in wonder of the time she holed an Empire wolfship and speared the captain with a single bolt.

Soulbane craves recognition from her peers and expects respect from Brackblood and his inner circle. She wants every corsair on the ark to know her name and secretly dreams of the day she commands her own ravenship, where she answers to none but the fleetmaster. Until then, she keeps on the good side of Captain Brackblood, and for each ship she sinks, carves a tally on her favourite captive’s back. 

Demeth is lean and angular, with dark blue eyes and her hair bound beneath a corsair’s helm. Her smirk is her signature expression, accompanied by a languid confidence that infuriates her peers.

## **Zarugh Kelvain, Eager Sailor**
Zarugh is a young dark elf possessing an unusual blend of youthful naïveté and courage that helps him survive amongst the Fell Brethren. As a mere sailor, the corsairs treat him with limited respect, but he has an instinct for spotting threats and an eager manner which leads others to underestimate him.

Zarugh yearns to become a corsair, dreaming of proving himself worthy of the sea dragon cloak he inherited from his dead mother. He wants to be seen as more than a boy, to stand alongside the Fell Brethren as a fellow reaver and earn Brackblood’s respect. Meanwhile, he toils on the foresail and climbs high above the deck to act as a lookout. 

Zarugh is a wiry young elf with alert eyes and black hair scraped back in a high sailor’s knot. His movements carry a nervous energy born from excitement and fear, and he speaks with an earnestness that masks surprising cunning. Those who meet Zarugh tend to assume he lacks guile, though he has learned to present a harmless façade for his own preservation.
